dimensions.note: The WireGuard private key and the SSH private key are sensitive-marked vault references. 2026.10.17.6 re-vendors the canonical ssh-host transport (blob 8f132c43) and drops the remote temp-file workaround: the key and config stream over ssh stdin into the script, which stages the key at 0600 under its own EXIT trap plus HUP/INT/TERM/PIPE traps, so a signalled run still removes it. No content-derived hash on any argv or script text. Live 7023c53: 0 hits for either WireGuard key, the SSH key or their sha256 in about 6,250 unique argv lines on both nodes and locally; 0 .ssh-host-upload*, wgmesh.* or .wg0.stage.* files after every cell, including hung and refused ones. Residual LOW: an armed rollback's backup holds a 0600 key copy under /etc/wireguard/.wg0.rollback.*/ for its 120 s window. README examples use vault references only (swamp-club lab 3555).
Each method logs once with the node name and outcome (changed / no change); no key material, config text or host keys in log fields.

SSH exit 255 is a typed TransportError; remote exit codes 75 (no flock), 3 (confirm after rollback) and 4 (superseded) map to typed errors. Every remote script now runs as `timeout -k 5 N sh -c <script>; exit $?` inside a surviving sh -c (TRIAGE 4f), N = ssh.command_timeout_s capped at 110 s, with a local deadline 15 s longer, so a hung step is killed remotely and reported (live cell 4: exit 124 after 24 s, lock freed). Residual LOW: the exit-124 error does not name the deadline. Residual MEDIUM (from .5): if wg-quick down and ip link delete both fail, delete removes the files before detecting the interface is still up (the armed rollback restores them).

128 unit/contract tests pass plus an opt-in netns suite (4 ignored without WG_MESH_NETNS=1), including a new netns cell that kills a session mid-apply with a hung wg-quick and asserts the rollback restores the baseline, a shell test that the rollback waits out a held lock, transport tests for the timeout -k 5 wrapper and the outliving local deadline, and the restored signal-trap test under sh. Live 2026.10.17.6 at 7023c53: 8/8 on two VPS (strict apply, no-op re-apply, armed revert, hung apply reverted twice, wrong pin, no remote secret temp files, argv scan, delete twice). The 2026.10.17.4 untested cells (self-severing delete, delete's own rollback firing) still block stable.

apply is a no-op when files, addresses and live peers match (live 2); delete again is a no-op (live 8); every live change arms a generation-checked rollback before mutating, disarmed only by a fresh-connection confirmation (live 3). The rollback now retries the node lock (flock -w 5, 900 s cap) instead of abandoning its generation, and the remote deadline frees the lock a hung body held, so a hung apply is reverted (live 4, twice). Runs are back to about 6 s (no-op about 3 s).

wg-quick / wg syncconf / wg set / ip, wireguard-tools 1.0.20210914 on Ubuntu 24.04 (live). Address or route changes recreate the interface; peer-only changes use syncconf. Drift is compared on the tool's own read-back (wg showconf peers, ip addr), not on the render text.

One flock per node, one SSH connection per step; the remote process group is killed at the deadline, so nothing outlives a run except the detached rollback, which removes its directory when the window ends (live). Residual LOW: delete leaves .wg0.epoch and .wg0.lock in /etc/wireguard; migrated 2026.10.17.4 per-node pin records stay in data.

Manifest @randybias/wireguard-mesh 2026.10.17.6, two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt; release stanza visibility public, audience general (naming answers in LOGBOOK, name kept). apply and delete are DESTRUCTIVE actions, delete requires acknowledge_reachability_risk=true; render and get are READ-ONLY. Leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass; branch history carries only RFC 5737 addresses; live receipts in LOGBOOK use redacted hosts.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject; every argument and resource schema is strict; keys, CIDRs, interface names, endpoints and host keys carry grammars and bounds; peers must be on peers_allowlist. New ssh.command_timeout_s is an integer 10..3600, default 300, described as capped at 110 s in effect. host_key_policy is strict | insecure_tofu; insecure is refused. Residual LOW: different spellings of one IPv6 address and a trailing-dot name get separate pins; host capitalization fails closed.
state infinite/10, rendered infinite/5, live infinite/5, hostkeys infinite/10.
render, apply (create or converge), get (live read-back) and delete (an action; deleting an absent interface is a no-op). No method uses kind delete, so no verb tombstones the definition.

Inputs, allowlist, relay exclusion and the delete acknowledgement are validated before any connection; the remote script refuses without flock (exit 75); host keys are passed to the canonical transport as authoritative pins, and a wrong pin refuses before any upload (live D). Under insecure_tofu the first accepted key is pinned for the rest of the operation and the confirmation connection uses it.

state, rendered and live are keyed by node name; host-key pins by <node>-hostkeys-<host>-<port>, so one definition serves every node and endpoint of a mesh without collision; a run against another host or port can no longer overwrite a pin.
Mesh data, SSH target and keys arrive as method arguments; the only data read back is this model's own host-key records (keyed, then the 2026.10.17.4 per-node record for the same endpoint).

upgrades[] carries a literal no-op entry for 2026.10.17.6 (adds the optional ssh.command_timeout_s input, no stored-attribute change) after the 2026.10.17.5 entry; the 2026.10.17.4 pin migration is unchanged and still unit-tested.
